output:
The panel used three independent lenses—patient behavior and access, small-clinic operations, and product/adoption experimentation—because no-shows can arise from different causes and constraints. It surfaced these unranked hypotheses:

| Direction | Value mechanism | Smallest discriminating experiment | Principal risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Patient-controlled reminders and visit previews | Let patients choose timing/channel; add calendar entry and concise purpose, preparation, duration, and cost information. | For one visit type, compare against standard reminders on attendance, confirmation, clarity, and opt-outs. | Notification fatigue, privacy exposure, or misleading generic information. |
| Frictionless cancel/reschedule | Turn an impending absence into an earlier cancellation or a valid rebooking through a one-step path into clinic-approved slots. | Offer a manually supported link to a small cohort; measure no-shows, completed rebookings, released lead time, and staff exceptions. | More cancellations without completed care, or invalid bookings from incomplete rules. |
| Optional barrier check-in | Surface transport, caregiving, work, language, mobility, or connectivity barriers and route only to support the clinic already offers—or to earlier rescheduling. | Ask one voluntary question and manually handle flagged cases; track resolved barriers, attendance, and staff minutes. | Intrusive disclosure, unmet expectations, or exclusion of patients who cannot use the channel. |
| Visit-readiness workflow | Show a simple checklist for forms, referrals, records, and preparation, sending only blocked cases to staff. | Pilot a three-item checklist for one appointment type; compare last-day unresolved cases, attendance, and follow-up time. | Incorrect status creates false reassurance or extra work. |
| Standby capacity exchange | Pair easy early cancellation with an opt-in standby queue that offers newly open slots in a bounded sequence. | Run a supervised list for one provider; measure early cancellations, fill rate, staff minutes, and offer disputes. | Eligibility conflicts or simultaneous offers create cleanup work; this may recover capacity without changing the root cause. |
| Commitment mechanisms | Test reciprocity first: the clinic states a realistic service-time promise and the patient explicitly confirms; separately, a voluntary refundable hold with a no-cost alternative explores whether a small stake changes behavior. | Pilot each variant independently in one limited session; measure attendance, timely cancellation, trust/objections, and whether the clinic keeps its promise. | Broken clinic promises erode trust; any financial hold can unfairly deter or burden patients. |

No direction is selected or ranked. Because the clinic segment and causes of nonattendance are unknown, each should remain a separate hypothesis; compare behavior change with staff workload and patient harms, not attendance alone.
